records.source: וַעֲזַרְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־עוֹדֵ֔ד הָיְתָ֥ה עָלָ֖יו ר֥וּחַ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And Azariah son of Oded, came on him [the] Spirit of God.
pieces: The Spirit of God came on Azariah son of Oded.

L.1: And Azariah son of Oded: the Spirit of God came on him.

R.1: The Spirit of God came on Azariah son of Oded.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God came on him: God moved him to speak as a prophet
decisions.reason: In Chronicles the Spirit comes on a person to give him a message from God, as on Amasai (1 Chronicles 12:19), Jahaziel (2 Chronicles 20:14) and Zechariah son of Jehoiada (24:20). What follows in verses 2-7 is Azariah's message, and verse 8 calls it a prophecy.

decisions.choice: Azariah son of Oded: a prophet named only in this chapter
decisions.reason: Nothing else is known of him or of his father. His name means "Yahweh has helped". He meets Asa as the king comes back from his victory over Zerah the Cushite (14:8-14).

decisions.choice: The Spirit of God came on Azariah son of Oded
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names Azariah first and then says "on him came the Spirit of God", putting the prophet in front. Literal keeps that order; Balanced and Readable say it in one plain clause.

records.heading: Azariah's message to Asa

records.source: וַיֵּצֵא֮ לִפְנֵ֣י אָסָא֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ שְׁמָע֕וּנִי אָסָ֖א וְכָל־יְהוּדָ֣ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ן יְהוָ֤ה עִמָּכֶם֙ בִּֽהְיֽוֹתְכֶ֣ם עִמּ֔וֹ וְאִֽם־תִּדְרְשֻׁ֨הוּ֙ יִמָּצֵ֣א לָכֶ֔ם וְאִם־תַּעַזְבֻ֖הוּ יַעֲזֹ֥ב אֶתְכֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And he went out before Asa and said to him, Hear me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin: Yahweh [is] with you when you are with him; and if you seek him he will be found by you, and if you forsake him he will forsake you.
pieces: He went out to meet Asa and spoke to him: "Hear me, Asa, and all of Judah and Benjamin. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is with you as long as you are with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. If you seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will let you find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; but if you abandon {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will abandon you.

L.2: And he went out before Asa and said to him, "Hear me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] with you while you are with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And if you seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be found by you; but if you forsake {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will forsake you.

R.2: He went out to meet Asa and said, "Listen to me, Asa, and all you people of Judah and Benjamin. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is with you as long as you stay with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. If you look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, you will find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But if you turn away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will turn away from you.

decisions.choice: went out before Asa: went out to meet him
decisions.reason: To go out "before" (literally "to the face of") someone is to go out to meet him. Asa is returning from the battle with Zerah (14:8-14).

decisions.choice: Yahweh is with you while you are with him: his help goes with their loyalty
decisions.reason: Asa had just seen Yahweh fight for him (14:10-12). Azariah tells the king and the people that Yahweh's presence and help are not automatic: they go with Judah's own faithfulness to him. The rest of the message and of Asa's story turns on this (16:7-9, 12).

decisions.choice: if you seek him he will be found by you; if you forsake him he will forsake you
decisions.reason: David says the same to Solomon in 1 Chronicles 28:9, "If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will reject you forever". Here the second half is "he will forsake you", the same verb said back of Yahweh, as at 12:5 and 24:20. Moses promised that Israel would find Yahweh when they sought him (Deuteronomy 4:29). Verses 4 and 15 tell how the promise came true.

decisions.choice: you: plural, the king and the people together
decisions.reason: Every "you" in the message is plural. Azariah speaks to Asa and to all Judah and Benjamin at once; what follows applies to the whole people.

decisions.choice: he will let you find him (Balanced); you will find him (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Chronicles 28:9. The Hebrew says "he will be found by you": God lets himself be found. Balanced keeps God as the one who acts; Readable says it from the seeker's side, which means the same.

decisions.choice: abandon (Balanced); turn away from (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one verb for both halves, "forsake ... forsake", and every level repeats one English verb to keep the matching sentence. Balanced uses "abandon" as at 1 Chronicles 28:9.

records.source: וְיָמִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְלֹ֣א׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֱמֶ֗ת וּלְלֹ֛א כֹּהֵ֥ן מוֹרֶ֖ה וּלְלֹ֥א תוֹרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And days many [were] for Israel without God of truth, and without priest teaching, and without law.
pieces: Israel went a long time without the true God, without a priest to teach, and without law.

L.3: And many days [were] for Israel without a true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.

R.3: For a long time Israel lived without the true God, without a priest to teach them, and without the law.

decisions.choice: a long time in the past, most likely the days of the judges
alternatives: of the present: the northern kingdom in Azariah's day
of the future: a warning of what will happen if they forsake Yahweh
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb: "many days to Israel without ...". It can be read of the past, of Azariah's own time, or of the future. Verses 4-6 use past-tense verbs and describe a time of disorder and turning back to Yahweh like the days of the judges (Judges 2:11-19; 21:25), so the record reads the past. Some read it of the northern kingdom in Azariah's day, cut off from the priests of Jerusalem (11:13-15; 13:9), or as a warning of what is to come, as Hosea 3:4 speaks of Israel living many days without king or sacrifice.

decisions.choice: a true God: the real God, who is faithful
decisions.reason: "God of truth" means the God who is real and keeps faith, as against gods that are nothing (Jeremiah 10:10). Israel was without him not because he left, but because they no longer knew or served him.

decisions.choice: a teaching priest; law: the instruction priests gave
decisions.reason: One of the priests' tasks was to teach Israel Yahweh's instruction (Leviticus 10:11; Deuteronomy 33:10; Malachi 2:7). The word for law is the same as "teaching" or "instruction": without priests who taught, the people did not know what Yahweh required. Jehoshaphat later sends priests and Levites through Judah to teach the book of the law (17:7-9).

decisions.choice: went ... without (Balanced); lived without (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply a past-tense verb, following the reading in m1. Literal brackets "were".

records.source: וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ בַּצַּר־ל֔וֹ עַל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְבַקְשֻׁ֖הוּ וַיִּמָּצֵ֥א לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: But turned in [the] distress of him to Yahweh God of Israel, and they sought him, and he was found by them.
pieces: But in their distress they turned back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel; they sought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let them find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.4: But in its distress [Israel] turned to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel, and they sought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was found by them.

R.4: But when they were in trouble, they turned back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. They looked for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: in distress Israel turned back to Yahweh: the pattern of the judges
decisions.reason: Again and again in Judges the people cried to Yahweh in their trouble and he raised up someone to rescue them (Judges 2:18; 3:9, 15; 10:10-16). Azariah reminds Asa that the promise of verse 2 has proved true before. The verbs may also describe what happened each time: whenever they turned back, he let them find him.

decisions.choice: it turned ... they sought: Israel as one people and as many
decisions.reason: The first verb is singular, with Israel (verse 3) as one people; the next is plural, the people together. Both mean the same people.

decisions.choice: they sought him and he was found by them
decisions.reason: The same words as the promise in verse 2. Verse 15 tells how it came true again for Asa's Judah.

decisions.choice: [Israel] (Literal); they (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. Literal names Israel in brackets; Balanced and Readable say "they", since the people are meant (m2). "Let them find him" and "found him" as in verse 2.

records.source: וּבָעִתִּ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין שָׁל֖וֹם לַיּוֹצֵ֣א וְלַבָּ֑א כִּ֚י מְהוּמֹ֣ת רַבּ֔וֹת עַ֥ל כָּל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י הָאֲרָצֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And in the times those there was no peace for the [one] going out and for the [one] coming in, for disturbances great [were] on all [the] inhabitants of the lands.
pieces: In those times there was no peace for anyone who went out or came in, because great turmoil troubled all who lived in those lands.

L.5: And in those times there was no peace for the [one] going out and for the [one] coming in, for great disturbances [were] on all the inhabitants of the lands.

R.5: In those days it was not safe to travel anywhere. All the people who lived in those lands were in great trouble and confusion.

decisions.choice: no peace for the one going out and the one coming in: no safety in daily life
decisions.reason: Going out and coming in takes in all the ordinary movement of life: travel, trade, work in the fields. In such times no one could go about safely, as in the days of Shamgar and Jael when the roads were deserted (Judges 5:6).

decisions.choice: great disturbances: turmoil and panic
decisions.reason: The word means uproar or confusion, often the panic Yahweh sends on his enemies (Deuteronomy 7:23; 1 Samuel 5:9). Verse 6 says that God himself sent it.

decisions.choice: the lands: the regions where Israel lived
decisions.reason: The plural may mean the territories of the tribes of Israel, or Israel and the neighboring countries together. Either way the disorder was everywhere.

decisions.choice: it was not safe to travel anywhere
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1) in plain words, and says "trouble and confusion" for the word in m2.

records.source: וְכֻתְּת֥וּ גוֹי־בְּג֖וֹי וְעִ֣יר בְּעִ֑יר כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֥ים הֲמָמָ֖ם בְּכָל־צָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they were crushed, nation by nation and city by city, for God troubled them with every distress.
pieces: Nation was crushed by nation and city by city, because God troubled them with every kind of distress.

L.6: And they were crushed, nation by nation and city by city, for God troubled them with every distress.

R.6: One nation crushed another, and one city crushed another, because God brought all kinds of trouble on them.

decisions.choice: crushed, nation by nation and city by city: they broke one another
alternatives: nation against nation and city against city
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "by" or "against". The sense is that peoples and towns fought and broke each other, not only that they suffered from outside enemies.

decisions.choice: God troubled them: the disorder was his judgment
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw into confusion, as Yahweh did to Egypt's army and to Israel's enemies (Exodus 14:24; Deuteronomy 7:23). Here he does it to his own people who had left him, as Judges 2:14-15 says.

decisions.choice: One nation crushed another, and one city crushed another
decisions.reason: Readable turns the passive into an active sentence and spells out the meaning in m1.

records.source: וְאַתֶּ֣ם חִזְק֔וּ וְאַל־יִרְפּ֖וּ יְדֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֛י יֵ֥שׁ שָׂכָ֖ר לִפְעֻלַּתְכֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And you, be strong and not let drop your hands, for there is reward for your work.
pieces: But as for you, be strong and do not let your hands go slack, for your work will be rewarded."

L.7: And you, be strong, and do not let your hands drop, for there is a reward for your work."

R.7: But you must be strong and not lose heart. What you do will be rewarded."

decisions.choice: do not let your hands drop: do not lose courage or give up
decisions.reason: Hands that hang down are a picture of weakness and losing heart (2 Samuel 4:1; Isaiah 13:7; Zephaniah 3:16). Azariah urges the king and people to keep going with the work of turning Judah back to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: there is a reward for your work
decisions.reason: The same words are found in Jeremiah 31:16, said to Rachel weeping for her children. Faithful work for Yahweh is not wasted: verse 15 tells of the rest that followed.

decisions.choice: and you: in contrast with those times
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed. After the picture of the past (verses 3-6), Azariah turns to Asa and the people: their time can be different.

decisions.choice: go slack (Balanced); not lose heart (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of hands with a natural verb; Readable gives the meaning (m1). Here the speech that began in verse 2 ends.

records.source: וְכִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אָסָ֜א הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְהַנְּבוּאָה֮ עֹדֵ֣ד הַנָּבִיא֒ הִתְחַזַּ֗ק וַיַּעֲבֵ֤ר הַשִּׁקּוּצִים֙ מִכָּל־אֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן וּמִן־הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָכַ֖ד מֵהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיְחַדֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֕ר לִפְנֵ֖י אוּלָ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And when heard Asa the words these and the prophecy, Oded the prophet, he took courage and removed the detestable things from all [the] land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities which he had captured from [the] hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed [the] altar of Yahweh which [was] before [the] porch of Yahweh.
pieces: When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he gathered his courage. He removed the detestable idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the towns he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim, and he repaired the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that stood in front of the porch of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

L.8: And when Asa heard these words and the prophecy [of] Oded the prophet, he took courage, and he removed the detestable things from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities that he had captured from [the] hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that [was] before the porch of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: When Asa heard these words, the message from the prophet Oded, he was encouraged. He got rid of the disgusting idols throughout the land of Judah and Benjamin, and from the towns he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. He also repaired the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in front of the porch of the temple.

decisions.choice: the prophecy, Oded the prophet: the text as it stands
alternatives: the prophecy of Azariah son of Oded the prophet
decisions.reason: Verse 1 names the speaker as Azariah son of Oded, but here the Hebrew text reads only "the prophecy, Oded the prophet". Some ancient translations (the Syriac and the Latin) read "Azariah son of Oded" here, and the words "Azariah son of" may have dropped out in copying. The record keeps the Hebrew text at every level; the prophecy meant is the one in verses 2-7.

decisions.choice: the detestable things: idols
decisions.reason: The word is used for idols and the objects of other gods' worship, always with disgust (Deuteronomy 29:16; 1 Kings 11:5, 7). It names the images Asa had begun to remove at the start of his reign (14:2-4).

decisions.choice: the towns he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim
decisions.reason: Chronicles does not tell of these captures. Abijah, Asa's father, had taken Bethel and other towns from Jeroboam (13:19), and 17:2 speaks of the towns of Ephraim that Asa captured, so the border with Israel had moved north into Ephraim's hill country.

decisions.choice: renewed the altar: restored the great altar of burnt offering
decisions.reason: The verb means to make new or restore. The altar "before the porch" is the bronze altar that stood in the courtyard in front of the temple porch (4:1; 8:12). Some sixty years after Solomon it needed repair, or had to be cleansed and rededicated for the sacrifices of verse 11.

decisions.choice: detestable idols (Balanced); disgusting idols (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "detestable things"; Balanced and Readable say what the things were (m2).

decisions.choice: the porch of the LORD's temple (Balanced); the porch of the temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the porch of Yahweh", meaning the porch of his house. Balanced and Readable name the temple so that the porch is not taken as something else; Readable also says "the message from the prophet Oded" for "the prophecy", which means the same.

records.heading: Asa renews the covenant

records.source: וַיִּקְבֹּ֗ץ אֶת־כָּל־יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן וְהַגָּרִים֙ עִמָּהֶ֔ם מֵאֶפְרַ֥יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וּמִשִּׁמְע֑וֹן כִּֽי־נָפְל֨וּ עָלָ֤יו מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל֙ לָרֹ֔ב בִּרְאֹתָ֕ם כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָ֖יו עִמּֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin and those sojourning with them from Ephraim and Manasseh and from Simeon, for they had fallen to him from Israel in abundance when they saw that Yahweh his God [was] with him.
pieces: He assembled all Judah and Benjamin, and the people from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon who were living among them as outsiders. Great numbers had deserted to him from Israel, because they saw that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God was with him.

L.9: And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and those sojourning with them from Ephraim and Manasseh and from Simeon, for they had fallen to him from Israel in abundance, when they saw that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God [was] with him.

R.9: He called together all the people of Judah and Benjamin, and the people from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon who had come to live among them. Large numbers of people had left Israel and come over to Asa, because they saw that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God was with him.

decisions.choice: those sojourning with them: people from the north living in Judah
decisions.reason: The verb means to live as an outsider in a place that is not one's home tribe or land. These were Israelites from the northern tribes who had settled in Judah, as the priests and Levites had done under Rehoboam (11:13-17).

decisions.choice: they had fallen to him: they had gone over to his side
decisions.reason: To "fall to" someone is to desert to him (1 Samuel 29:3; 2 Kings 25:11). They left the northern kingdom for Judah.

decisions.choice: Simeon: a tribe whose land lay inside Judah's
decisions.reason: Simeon's towns were in the far south, within Judah's territory (Joshua 19:1-9). That people of Simeon came "from Israel" may mean some Simeonites had settled in the north, or that Simeon was counted among the northern tribes after the kingdom divided.

decisions.choice: Yahweh his God was with him
decisions.reason: What drew them is the truth of verse 2: Yahweh was with Asa, as his victory over Zerah showed (14:8-14).

decisions.choice: living among them as outsiders (Balanced); had come to live among them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sojourning", the verb related to the noun "sojourner"; Balanced uses "outsiders" as for that noun in these books. Readable breaks the long sentence and names Asa for "him".

records.source: וַיִּקָּבְצ֥וּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י לִשְׁנַ֥ת חֲמֵשׁ־עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה לְמַלְכ֥וּת אָסָֽא׃
records.gloss: And they gathered [at] Jerusalem in the month the third of [the] year fifteen of [the] reign of Asa.
pieces: They assembled at Jerusalem in the third month of Asa's fifteenth year as king.

L.10: And they gathered [at] Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.

R.10: They gathered in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year that Asa was king.

decisions.choice: the third month: late spring, the time of the Festival of Weeks
decisions.reason: The third month (later called Sivan) fell in May and June, at the end of the grain harvest. The Festival of Weeks was kept then (Exodus 23:16; Leviticus 23:15-21). The festival's name and the "oath" of verses 14-15 sound alike in Hebrew, and the gathering may have been timed for the festival, but the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: the fifteenth year of Asa's reign
decisions.reason: Asa had ten quiet years at the start of his reign (13:23), and then defeated Zerah (14:8-14). The assembly comes soon after that victory, with the plunder still at hand (verse 11).

decisions.choice: the fifteenth year that Asa was king
decisions.reason: Readable says "that Asa was king" for "of the reign of Asa", as with the other dates in these books.

records.source: וַיִּזְבְּח֤וּ לַיהוָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא מִן־הַשָּׁלָ֖ל הֵבִ֑יאוּ בָּקָר֙ שְׁבַ֣ע מֵא֔וֹת וְצֹ֖אן שִׁבְעַ֥ת אֲלָפִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they sacrificed to Yahweh on the day that from the plunder [that] they had brought: cattle seven hundred and sheep seven thousand.
pieces: On that day they sacrificed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the plunder they had brought back: 700 cattle and 7,000 sheep.

L.11: And they sacrificed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on that day from the plunder [that] they had brought: 700 cattle and 7,000 sheep.

R.11: That day they offered sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the animals they had captured and brought back: 700 cattle and 7,000 sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: the plunder they had brought: the livestock taken in the war with Zerah
decisions.reason: After the victory over Zerah the Cushite, Judah carried off sheep, goats and camels in great numbers from the land around Gerar (14:12-14). Part of it is now given back to Yahweh, who had won the battle.

decisions.choice: sheep: the word covers sheep and goats
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means a flock of small animals, sheep and goats together.

decisions.choice: the animals they had captured; sheep and goats
decisions.reason: Readable says what the plunder was (m1) and names both kinds of animal in the flock (m2).

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ בַבְּרִ֔ית לִדְר֕וֹשׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם בְּכָל־לְבָבָ֖ם וּבְכָל־נַפְשָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And they entered into [the] covenant to seek Yahweh God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul,
pieces: They entered into the covenant: they would seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and with all their soul,

L.12: And they entered into the covenant to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul,

R.12: They made a covenant to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and with all their being.

decisions.choice: entered into a covenant: bound themselves by solemn agreement
decisions.reason: To "enter into" a covenant is to take it on oneself with its promises and penalties (Deuteronomy 29:11; Jeremiah 34:10). This is not a new covenant with Yahweh but a renewal of the people's commitment to the one he made with Israel. The article may point to that covenant: "the covenant".

decisions.choice: seek Yahweh: turn to him, worship him and ask his will
decisions.reason: To seek Yahweh in Chronicles is to make him the one God served, worshiped and asked for help, as against other gods (1 Chronicles 10:13-14; 2 Chronicles 14:3). It is the key word of Azariah's message (verse 2).

decisions.choice: with all their heart and with all their soul
decisions.reason: The words of Deuteronomy 4:29, where Moses promised that Israel would find Yahweh when they sought him with all their heart and all their soul, and of the great command to love him so (Deuteronomy 6:5). Heart and soul together mean the whole person.

decisions.choice: ancestors; being (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers". Readable says "being" for "soul" as at Deuteronomy 4:29, since the Hebrew means the whole self. The sentence goes on in verse 13; Literal and Balanced end this verse with a comma, and Readable starts a new sentence.

records.source: וְכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יִדְרֹ֛שׁ לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יוּמָ֑ת לְמִן־קָטֹן֙ וְעַד־גָּד֔וֹל לְמֵאִ֖ישׁ וְעַד־אִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: and every [one] who not will seek Yahweh God of Israel will be put to death, from small to great, from man to woman.
pieces: and anyone, young or old, man or woman, who refused to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, would be put to death.

L.13: and every [one] who would not seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel would be put to death, from small to great, from man to woman.

R.13: Anyone who would not seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, whether young or old, man or woman.

decisions.choice: whoever would not seek Yahweh would be put to death
decisions.reason: The covenant takes up the law against turning to other gods, which named death for anyone who did so, whether a family member, a whole town, or any man or woman (Exodus 22:19; Deuteronomy 13:7-12; 17:2-7). Not seeking Yahweh here means refusing him for other gods, not lacking zeal.

decisions.choice: from small to great, from man to woman: everyone without exception
decisions.reason: Two pairs of opposites take in the whole people: young and old (or low and high) and men and women. No one is exempt.

decisions.choice: and anyone, young or old, man or woman, who refused to seek
decisions.reason: Balanced carries on the sentence from verse 12, where the colon introduces what the covenant said, and moves the pairs of opposites forward so that the sentence ends on its main point. "Refused to seek" says "would not seek" as a choice, which is the sense (m1).

decisions.choice: young or old
decisions.reason: "Small" and "great" can mean young and old or humble and important; Balanced and Readable say "young or old", the usual sense when set beside "man or woman".

records.source: וַיִּשָּֽׁבְעוּ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה בְּק֥וֹל גָּד֖וֹל וּבִתְרוּעָ֑ה וּבַחֲצֹצְר֖וֹת וּבְשׁוֹפָרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And they swore to Yahweh with a voice loud and with shouting and with trumpets and with horns.
pieces: They swore an oath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with a loud voice, with shouts of joy, and with trumpets and rams' horns.

L.14: And they swore to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets, and with horns.

R.14: They made their promise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with loud voices. They shouted for joy and blew trumpets and rams' horns.

decisions.choice: shouting, trumpets and horns: the sounds of a great festival
decisions.reason: The shout could be a war cry or a cry of joy; here, with verse 15, it is joy. The trumpets were the metal trumpets the priests blew at festivals and sacrifices (Numbers 10:2-10; 1 Chronicles 15:24); the horns were rams' horns, used for signals and celebrations, as when the ark was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 15:28).

decisions.choice: swore: took a solemn oath
decisions.reason: They bound themselves by oath to keep the covenant of verses 12-13.

decisions.choice: swore an oath; shouts of joy; rams' horns
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "oath" or "promise" as the object of the verb, say what kind of shouting it was (m1), and name the horns as rams' horns.

records.source: וַיִּשְׂמְח֨וּ כָל־יְהוּדָ֜ה עַל־הַשְּׁבוּעָ֗ה כִּ֤י בְכָל־לְבָבָם֙ נִשְׁבָּ֔עוּ וּבְכָל־רְצוֹנָ֣ם בִּקְשֻׁ֔הוּ וַיִּמָּצֵ֖א לָהֶ֑ם וַיָּ֧נַח יְהוָ֛ה לָהֶ֖ם מִסָּבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And rejoiced all Judah over the oath, for with all their heart they had sworn, and with all their will they had sought him, and he was found by them; and gave rest Yahweh to them from around.
pieces: All Judah rejoiced over the oath, because they had sworn it with all their heart and had sought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all their desire, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let them find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them rest on every side.

L.15: And all Judah rejoiced over the oath, for with all their heart they had sworn, and with all their desire they had sought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was found by them; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them rest from all around.

R.15: All the people of Judah were glad about the promise, because they had made it with all their heart. They had looked for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all their desire, and they found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them peace on every side.

decisions.choice: they had sought him and he was found by them: the promise kept
decisions.reason: The very words of Azariah's promise (verse 2) and of the past (verse 4). Because the people sought Yahweh wholeheartedly, he let them find him.

decisions.choice: with all their desire: with their whole will, gladly
decisions.reason: The word means will, desire or goodwill. With "all their heart" it says that the oath was not forced but freely and gladly taken.

decisions.choice: gave them rest from all around: peace from enemies on every side
decisions.reason: Rest is the peace Yahweh promised when Israel was secure from its enemies (Deuteronomy 12:10; 1 Chronicles 22:9). Chronicles said the same of Asa's early years (14:5-6), and verse 19 tells how long it lasted.

decisions.choice: he let them find him (Balanced); they found him (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verses 2 and 4. Readable says "peace" for "rest" (m3), and "promise" for "oath" as in verse 14.

records.source: וְגַֽם־מַעֲכָ֞ה אֵ֣ם׀אָסָ֣א הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הֱסִירָהּ֙ מִגְּבִירָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשְׂתָ֥ה לַאֲשֵׁרָ֖ה מִפְלָ֑צֶת וַיִּכְרֹ֤ת אָסָא֙ אֶת־מִפְלַצְתָּ֔הּ וַיָּ֕דֶק וַיִּשְׂרֹ֖ף בְּנַ֥חַל קִדְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And also Maacah [the] mother of Asa the king, he removed her from [being] queen mother, because she had made for Asherah a horrid thing; and cut down Asa her horrid thing and crushed and burned [it] in [the] valley of Kidron.
pieces: King Asa even deposed his mother Maacah as queen mother, because she had made a horrid image for Asherah. Asa cut down her image, crushed it and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

L.16: And also Maacah, the mother of Asa the king: he removed her from [being] queen mother, because she had made a horrid thing for Asherah; and Asa cut down her horrid thing and crushed [it] and burned [it] in the valley of Kidron.

R.16: King Asa even took away the title of queen mother from Maacah, his mother, because she had made a disgusting idol to worship the goddess Asherah. Asa cut the idol down, crushed it and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

decisions.choice: the same account as 1 Kings 15:13, with two differences
decisions.reason: Verses 16-18 repeat 1 Kings 15:13-15 almost word for word. Here Maacah is "the mother of Asa the king" where Kings has "his mother", and Asa "crushed" the object before burning it, a word Kings does not have.

decisions.choice: mother: probably his grandmother, who stayed queen mother
decisions.reason: Maacah was the wife of Rehoboam and the mother of Abijah, Asa's father (11:20-22). "Mother" here most likely means grandmother, who kept her place as queen mother into Asa's reign. Chronicles names Abijah's mother as Micaiah daughter of Uriel at 13:2, which may be another form of her name.

decisions.choice: queen mother: an office at the royal court
decisions.reason: The word means "great lady". The king's mother held a recognized place of honor and influence (1 Kings 2:19; Jeremiah 13:18). Asa took that position away from Maacah, as 1 Kings 15:13 explains.

decisions.choice: a horrid thing for Asherah: an object of worship meant to cause horror
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to shudder, and it is found only here and in 1 Kings 15:13. What it looked like is not known; that it was cut down suggests wood, or a pole. Asherah was a Canaanite goddess, and the same word names the wooden poles set up for her, but "for Asherah" points to the goddess.

decisions.choice: the valley of Kidron: the valley on the east side of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: A stream bed east of the city that runs only in the rainy season. Kings who cleansed Judah of idols destroyed them there (29:16; 30:14; 2 Kings 23:4, 6).

decisions.choice: horrid image (Balanced); disgusting idol (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 15:13. Literal keeps "horrid thing"; Readable says who Asherah was (m4). Balanced and Readable move "King Asa" to the front of the sentence.

records.source: וְהַ֨בָּמ֔וֹת לֹא־סָ֖רוּ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל רַ֧ק לְבַב־אָסָ֛א הָיָ֥ה שָׁלֵ֖ם כָּל־יָמָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And the high places not were removed from Israel; only [the] heart of Asa was whole all his days.
pieces: The high places, however, were not taken away from Israel. Even so, Asa's heart was undivided all his life.

L.17: But the high places were not removed from Israel; only, the heart of Asa was whole all his days.

R.17: But the hilltop shrines were not removed from Israel. Even so, Asa was completely loyal to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all his life.

decisions.choice: the same verdict as 1 Kings 15:14, with two differences
decisions.reason: Kings says the high places were not removed, and that Asa's heart was whole "with Yahweh". Chronicles adds "from Israel" and leaves out "with Yahweh", though his loyalty to Yahweh is still the point.

decisions.choice: from Israel: perhaps the northern territory Asa held
decisions.reason: Chronicles has said that Asa removed the high places from the towns of Judah (14:2, 4). "From Israel" may mean the towns he had taken from the northern kingdom (verse 8), so the two statements agree; or "Israel" may mean the whole people, and the earlier removal was not complete.

decisions.choice: his heart was whole: his loyalty was undivided
decisions.reason: A whole or complete heart is one given without reserve, as in 1 Chronicles 28:9. Though the high places stayed, Asa himself served Yahweh with an undivided heart.

decisions.choice: high places (Literal, Balanced); hilltop shrines (Readable); Even so
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in these books, as at 1 Kings 15:14. Balanced says "undivided", since Chronicles does not have "with Yahweh" here.

decisions.choice: completely loyal to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the one Asa was loyal to, which the sentence leaves to be understood (m1).

records.source: וַיָּבֵ֞א אֶת־קָדְשֵׁ֥י אָבִ֛יו וְקָֽדָשָׁ֖יו בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כֶּ֥סֶף וְזָהָ֖ב וְכֵלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he brought [the] holy things of his father and his holy things [into the] house of the God: silver and gold and vessels.
pieces: He brought into the house of God the gifts his father had dedicated and the gifts he himself had dedicated: silver, gold and utensils.

L.18: And he brought the holy things of his father and his holy things [into] the house of God: silver and gold and vessels.

R.18: He brought into God's temple the gifts of silver and gold and other objects that his father and he himself had dedicated to God.

decisions.choice: the same as 1 Kings 15:15, with "God" for "Yahweh"
decisions.reason: Kings has "the house of Yahweh"; Chronicles says "the house of God". Here the Hebrew plainly reads "his holy things", Asa's own gifts, the reading followed at 1 Kings 15:15.

decisions.choice: holy things: gifts dedicated to God
decisions.reason: Things declared holy belonged to God and were kept in the temple treasuries, often silver and gold taken in war (1 Chronicles 18:11; 26:26-27). Abijah's may have come from his war with Jeroboam (13:16-19), Asa's from the war with Zerah (14:12-14).

decisions.choice: [into]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no preposition: the house is the place the gifts were brought to.

decisions.choice: God's temple; dedicated to God
decisions.reason: Readable calls the house of God the temple and explains "holy things" as dedicated gifts (m2).

records.source: וּמִלְחָמָ֖ה לֹ֣א הָיָ֑תָה עַ֛ד שְׁנַת־שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְחָמֵ֖שׁ לְמַלְכ֥וּת אָסָֽא׃ס
records.gloss: And war not was until [the] year thirty and five of [the] reign of Asa.
pieces: There was no war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.

L.19: And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.

R.19: There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year that Asa was king.

decisions.choice: the thirty-fifth year: a date hard to fit with Kings
alternatives: counted from the division of the kingdom
a copying error for an earlier year
decisions.reason: According to 1 Kings 15:33 Baasha became king of Israel in Asa's third year and reigned twenty-four years, and 1 Kings 16:8 has his son Elah succeed him in Asa's twenty-sixth year. Yet 16:1 here dates Baasha's attack in Asa's thirty-sixth year, and 1 Kings 15:16 speaks of war between Asa and Baasha all their days. The number may count from the division of the kingdom, so that "the reign of Asa" means the kingdom of Judah he ruled, which would put the war about Asa's fifteenth or sixteenth year; or a number may have been miscopied (for example from fifteen or twenty-five); or Chronicles may be using its own reckoning. The record keeps the text as written.

decisions.choice: no war: the rest Yahweh gave
decisions.reason: The years of peace are the rest of verse 15, given because Judah sought Yahweh. Chapter 16 tells how Asa later relied on Aram instead of on Yahweh, and war returned (16:9).

decisions.choice: no more war
decisions.reason: Readable adds "more", since Judah had just fought Zerah (14:8-14) and the verse speaks of the years after that war.
